author: reek
body: Ray-tracing reflections as a [Device] compute kernel: the same three-sphere, checkered-floor scene as the ray tracer, but every surface is a mirror. Each pixel traces a primary ray, shades the nearest hit locally (diffuse + hard shadow), then reflects the ray about the surface normal and traces one more bounce, blending the reflected colour in by the surface's reflectivity. This is the reference site's "ray tracing reflections" technique, from Codex AST.

author: reek
body: The local shade is a shared helper (rf-local) reused for both the primary hit and the reflected hit; the reflected colour is unpacked back to floats and blended. Nearest-hit and shadow tests are tail-recursive folds the plug lowers to WGSL loops. Real math from Gpu chapter DeviceMath.

author: reek
body: Local shade of the hit on object id along ray (ox,oy,oz)+(dx,dy,dz): Lambert from a rotating key light plus a hard shadow ray. No reflection here -- that is composited by rf-render. Returns a packed colour.
